conditions: Terms §4 says resale/sublicensing is prohibited except as expressly permitted by an Enterprise agreement; lifetime terms §6 require a separate Enterprise reseller agreement and exclude resale/white-label from lifetime seats. Self-serve and lifetime are not qualifying plans.

Executed Enterprise agreement/order form must state Vrooli's downstream application/customer scope, customer key/account architecture, brand, model families/endpoints, limits, pricing, service commitments and rights/precedence.

Plugsky supplies hosted routing but Terms §7 name opencode.ai, NVIDIA NIM and others as underlying providers. Identify the actual provider for each route and confirm its terms and model publisher/license separately.
Confirm current catalog and route availability, fair-use limits, data/DPA, trust/regions, SLA remedies and upstream failure responsibility. Self-serve price list is not Enterprise reseller pricing.
Provider agreement/rule, exact models, trust and Vrooli price require separate human decisions; no route is enabled by this proposal.
plan_rules.reason: Official Terms condition service resale on an Enterprise agreement; official lifetime terms state own-use only and describe an Enterprise reseller agreement. This supports a conditional Enterprise candidate only.

source_anchors.supports: Terms §4 permits service resale/sublicense only as expressly allowed by an Enterprise agreement.
source_anchors.does_not_establish: This source does not establish executed supplier approval or agreement, the exact Vrooli account entitlement, actual upstream serving provider/model rights, a live route, customer trust terms, or a human-approved price.

source_anchors.supports: Lifetime Terms §6–8 exclude resale/white-label rights absent the separate Enterprise agreement.
source_anchors.does_not_establish: This public source does not establish an executed agreement for Vrooli, account entitlement, exact model-level upstream rights, or an approved route.

research.model_reason: Plugsky's model/catalog tags do not establish the active upstream serving provider or that provider's downstream permission; provider terms apply per route.
